title: Consumption Resilience Toolkit — Product Brief
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
-------
This brief describes the Consumption Resilience Toolkit (CRT), a product initiative to give customers predictable application behavior and bounded costs when runtime capacity, model variants, or regions become constrained. CRT combines runtime routing policies, credit-backed fallback economics, and a lightweight SDK to make graceful degradation transparent and actionable for application owners.

Why this matters
-----------------
- Customers increasingly run mission-critical flows (search, summarization, assistant agents) where a sudden drop in fidelity or a model-fallback spike in cost causes user-visible regressions and business impact.
- Existing fallback behaviors are either opaque to customers or shift unexpected cost/latency tradeoffs back to them.
- A unified toolkit reduces churn, shortens incident MTTR, and enables revenue-grade SLAs for hosted and dedicated deployments.

Goals and success metrics
-------------------------
Primary goals:
1. Reduce customer-visible fidelity regressions caused by capacity events by 60% within the first 6 months after rollout (measured by regression alerts and shadow-eval mismatches).
2. Limit unplanned consumption cost spikes on fallback events to < 20% of baseline per-customer on average.
3. Provide clear integration path for customers so 40% of Dedicated customers adopt CRT policies within 9 months.
4. Support both hosted and Private (VPC) deployments with the same runtime contracts.

Success metrics (examples):
- Fidelity-regression-rate (monthly): baseline 4.0% -> target 1.6%
- Median failover time to fallback variant: < 200 ms
- Cost spike rate during failover events: < 20% of normal monthly delta
- Customer adoption: percentage of active tenants with CRT policy attached to at least one route

Key features and user-facing flows
---------------------------------
1) Policy Builder (Console + API)
   - Create per-route policies: prefer-by-latency, prefer-by-cost, hybrid (latency-weighted cost cap).
   - Policy knobs: fallbackVariantList (ordered), credit-buffer-percent (0–200%), max-cost-multiplier, regional-preference, allow-preemptible
   - Preflight simulator: run a 10k-sample simulation against historical tenant traces to estimate cost and fidelity impact.

2) Credit-backed Fallbacks
   - Customers can provision a small resilience-credit pool (converted from token/compute credits) that pays for higher-cost fallbacks during constrained windows.
   - When credits deplete, policy enters degraded mode (rate-limited fallbacks, reduced token budgets) and triggers telemetry hooks to the customer.

3) Predictive Routing Oracle
   - A hybrid classifier in the control plane that tags routes with short-term risk estimates (healthy | at-risk | constrained) based on capacity signals, queue depths, and pricing signals.
   - Policies can refer to oracle tags to proactively switch variants before SLOs are breached.

4) SDK + Integration Kit
   - Lightweight SDK for Node/Python/Go enabling: local preflight checks, local cost estimation for generated tokens, and telemetry hooks for automatic incident annotations.
   - Example guardrail: if predicted fallback cost > 1.5x baseline, SDK returns a 429-like error plus structured metadata so application can present an in-product notice.

5) Observability and Billing Hooks
   - Per-tenant dashboards: fallback frequency, credit burn rate, variant fidelity delta, and cost attribution at token-level.
   - Billing integrations emit a per-fallback-event record for downstream invoicing and chargeback.

Architecture and runtime contract
--------------------------------
- Lightweight control plane service (crt-control): stores policies, evaluates route decisions, interfaces with the Predictive Routing Oracle, emits decision traces. Ownership: Runtime Platform team.
- Runtime agent (crt-agent) deployed alongside serving nodes: enforces variant routing decisions, interacts with local cache/batching for fallback warmups. Ownership: Serving Runtime team.
- SDK (crt-sdk): client-side guardrails and telemetry. Ownership: Developer Experience team.

Runtime contract (summary):
- Policy evaluation is best-effort and idempotent. Decisions include: allow, prefer-variant-X, delay (ms), charge-credit (units).
- Decision traces are emitted synchronously to the trace pipeline with a CRT tag (trace.sample_rate = 1% by default).
- CRT must guarantee no request dropped silently: application either receives primary response, fallback response, or a structured failure with reason.

SLOs and pricing implications
------------------------------
SLOs (for CRT control plane):
- Policy evaluation latency (p95): < 12 ms
- Decision sync to runtime-agents (p99): < 150 ms for regional clusters
- Credit accounting consistency window: eventual within 2 minutes; strong consistency for reserve operations

Pricing model proposals (high level):
- Base: CRT policy attachment is free for hosted tiers; customers pay only for credits consumed and additional variant cost delta.
- Credits: sold as monthly bundles (small: $50, medium: $500, large: $5,000) with conversion to internal compute units.
- Enterprise add-on: SLA-backed CRT with revenue-share on variant premium if provider-provisioned warm capacity is used.

Commercial implications and guardrails:
- Allow customers to preview monthly "stressed cost" estimate in Console before enabling policy.
- Default policy for free-tier accounts should be conservative (no auto-fallback to higher-cost variants without explicit opt-in).

Rollout plan and phases
------------------------
Phase 0 — Lab (Q2 2026)
- Implement crt-control prototype, crt-agent proof-of-concept, and SDK alpha.
- Run internal red-team scenarios and evaluate on 5 synthetic tenant traces.

Phase 1 — Beta (Q3 2026)
- Invite 10 pilot customers (mix of Hosted and Dedicated).
- Collect telemetry, refine cost-conversion tables, and onboard Billing hooks.
- Deliver Console policy builder v0 and preflight simulator.

Phase 2 — GA (Q4 2026)
- GA release with default policies, credit bundles, and integration guides.
- 90-day commercial pilot program for enterprise clients with SLA add-on.

Phase 3 — Scale (2027)
- Expand oracle signals (region-level pricing arbitrage, third-party capacity), optimize p95 decision latency, and add richer SDK features (local emulation).

Integration and migration guidance
---------------------------------
- Default adoption path for Hosted customers: opt-in via Console -> run preflight simulation -> enable on a test route -> migrate primary traffic after 2 weeks of allowable rollback window.
- Dedicated/Private customers: CRT can run in a hybrid mode where crt-control is hosted and crt-agent runs in-customer VPC with explicit networking (mTLS). Documented network ports and firewall rules are in the Appendix.

Operational playbook (incidents)
--------------------------------
1. Incident detection: crt-control emits "oracle:constraining" alerts when risk score moves to constrained.
2. Triage steps:
   a) Verify decision traces for affected tenants.
   b) If credit exhaustion caused spikes, run emergency credit top-up for critical tenants (manual steps in Billing Runbook).
   c) If oracle misprediction, revert to static policy and file a model-calibration postmortem.
3. Communication: notify customers with the pre-configured incident template and include structured CRT trace IDs for debugging.

Ownership and team responsibilities
----------------------------------
- Product: Aisha Patel (product lead), responsible for roadmap, commercial packaging, and pilot coordination.
- Runtime Platform: owns crt-control and oracle integration.
- Serving Runtime: owns crt-agent, variant warmups, and runtime enforcement.
- Developer Experience: owns SDK and Console UX.
- Billing: owns credit bundles, invoicing hooks, and chargeback records.

Dependencies and risks
----------------------
- Dependencies: Trace and metrics pipeline (p99 ingest), Billing feature to support micro-event charges, dedicated warm capacity marketplace.
- Risks: inaccurate oracle predictions causing unnecessary premium consumption; telemetry volume growth; customer confusion over credit semantics.

Customer-facing artifacts and docs
----------------------------------
- Console policy builder UX with presets and a one-click preflight simulator.
- Integration guide: CRT SDK quickstart (Node/Python/Go), sample error handling patterns.
- Commercial playbook: default bundles, negotiation anchors for SLA add-ons, pilot discount templates.
- FAQ: clear answers about credits, refunds, and data residency for Private deployments.

Appendix A — Example policy JSON
--------------------------------
{
  "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "policy_name": "balanced-low-cost",
  "fallbackVariantList": ["redwood-base-q4-1.2b", "redwood-quant-1.2b"],
  "credit_buffer_percent": "25",
  "max_cost_multiplier": "1.4",
  "regional_preference": "same-region"
}

Appendix B — Example SDK error payload (trimmed)
-------------------------------------------------
{
  "code": "CRT_FALLBACK_BLOCKED",
  "message": "Predicted fallback cost exceeds tenant-configured threshold",
  "metadata": {
    "predicted_multiplier": "1.72",
    "recommended_action": "decrease_max_tokens_or_retry_later",
    "crt_trace_id": "crt-20260407-xyzt"
  }
}

Appendix C — Network & security notes (Dedicated/Private)
---------------------------------------------------------
- CRT agents communicate with crt-control over mTLS on port 443 by default.
- For Private air-gapped deployments, a local oracle shim can be provided; roadmap item for Q1 2027.

Open questions
--------------
1. What should the default credit-to-compute conversion ratio be for mixed GPU fleets? (pricing & infra decision required).
2. Do we enable auto-topup for credits by default for enterprise customers, or require explicit approval?
3. How do we surface cross-tenant warmup subsidies in multi-tenant warm pools without causing billing disputes?

Next steps
----------
- Align on conversion ratio with Finance and Infra teams (owner: Product & Finance) by 2026-05-30.
- Build crt-control alpha and run internal red-team scenarios (owner: Runtime Platform) by 2026-07-31.
- Recruit pilot customers and finalize Console UX for preflight simulator (owner: Developer Experience) by 2026-08-30.
